claims.wording: Micromat advertises Techtool Pro 21 for Mac diagnostics, troubleshooting and repair.
claims.excerpt: Techtool Pro provides complete Mac diagnostics, plus a host of troubleshooting and repair tools.
claims.location: comparison identity and article diagnostic branch
claims.conditions: Do not repeat complete as a tested coverage guarantee.

claims.wording: The vendor lists Apple Silicon and Intel Macs and macOS 13.5 Ventura through its stated macOS 27 Golden Gate upper bound.
claims.excerpt: System Requirements: Apple Silicon and Intel-based Macs macOS 13.5 ‘Ventura’ through macOS 27 ‘Golden Gate’
claims.conditions: Upper OS name/version is quoted vendor wording, not independently verified Apple release identity or tested compatibility. Exact patch/build and hardware feature restrictions unknown.

claims.wording: The standard offer is a one-time, one-computer purchase with one year of updates; annual subscriptions are also offered.
claims.excerpt: One time purchase Licensed for one computer ... The standard license provides updates for one year from the date of purchase. A new license can be purchased at the end of that year to continue receiving updates.
claims.conditions: Not a lifetime-update promise. Actual EULA not inspected; no open-source license inferred.

claims.wording: The observed localized page displayed Standard 110,00 $, Subscription 80,00 $ initially and 90,00 $ on renewal, and eligible non-subscription-user upgrade 67,50 $ initially then 90,00 $ annually.
claims.excerpt: Techtool Pro Subscription Upgrade ... 90,00 $ ... 67,50 $ ... For non-subscription Techtool Pro users ... Renews every year. 90,00 $ per year for subsequent years. ... Techtool Pro Subscription ... 90,00 $ ... 80,00 $ ... 10% off first year ... Techtool Pro Standard ... 110,00 $
claims.conditions: Retained text uses nonbreaking spaces. Currency code not explicit; do not call USD or final tax-inclusive prices. 10% headline conflicts with displayed 90-to-80 reduction. Do not calculate savings, harmonize amounts or promise checkout price. One computer; extra licenses in cart; no cart opened.

claims.wording: Micromat says single- and three-Mac subscriptions from version 18.1.2 continue functioning after expiry, without further updates and with a resubscription reminder.
claims.excerpt: starting with version 18.1.2, Techtool Pro will continue to function once the subscription lapses for single and 3-Mac licenses. ... When your subscription ends, updates will no longer be available, and there will be a reminder to re-subscribe
claims.conditions: Do not extend to enterprise packs. Product page limits cancel-any-time wording to 1 and 3 user licenses.

claims.wording: Documented tests include memory, drive structures, fans/sensors, files and battery; custom Check Computer suites are offered.
claims.excerpt: Advanced Memory Testing ... Fans and Sensors ... File Testing ... Battery Testing ... Use the built-in Full, Intermediate or Quick suites or make your own suite of tests
claims.conditions: No tests were run; not all hardware/test combinations established.

claims.wording: Techtool Pro documents Mac volume testing/repair and FAT32/ExFAT testing/repair; its APFS support article qualifies repair and excludes APFS file/volume optimization.
claims.excerpt: can validate APFS volumes using the Volume Structures test and may potentially repair APFS structure errors using the Volume Rebuild tool. ... The only features that Techtool Pro doesn’t support for APFS volumes are the File and Volume Optimization tools. ... a full rebuild that reorganizes the volume structures can only be implemented once Apple provides further documentation.
claims.conditions: Do not promise recovery, full APFS rebuild, SSD defragmentation benefits, or a Windows app. Support article does not identify current patch scope; keep vendor qualification attached.

claims.wording: The product page documents system database repairs and clearing problem caches.
claims.excerpt: It can repair important system database files, clear out problem caches, and even check your apps and security settings for issues.
claims.conditions: Specific developer cache adapters, exact-path approval controls and reversibility are not verified; do not label them absent.

claims.wording: Techtool Monitor is documented as a background agent that monitors SMART, volume usage/APFS snapshots, processor frequency/power and battery/UPS health, with configurable email alerts.
claims.excerpt: protection doesn’t stop when you close the app. This background agent ... monitors SMART health data ... tracks volume usage ... keeps an eye on APFS snapshots ... CPU, tracking frequency and power usage over time ... battery — or a connected UPS ... simply configure your email settings
claims.conditions: Not evidence of per-app helper grouping or recurring-folder writer attribution. No monitoring or email configuration performed.

claims.wording: Micromat says installed software is governed by the license supplied at installation and store purchases include applicable sales tax based on shipping address.
claims.excerpt: Your use of Micromat-branded software is on the terms of the license in effect for the software at the time of purchase. ... Sales Tax. Micromat purchases will include sales tax based on your shipping address
claims.conditions: No installer/EULA, activation, trial, sign-in requirement, signing/notarization, runtime dependency or offline-activation test performed.

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a free Apache-2.0 macOS maintenance preview; the identified release is 0.1.0-preview.1 for macOS 13+ with an advertised universal installer.
claims.excerpt: Published preview says Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized ... Python 3.10+ is a disclosed prerequisite ... Physical Intel behavior remains explicitly untested.
claims.conditions: No clean-machine/physical-Intel test or distributed binary parity verification; do not recommend bypassing protections.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source supports storage exploration, grouped app/process CPU-memory views, activity history and constrained local cleanup actions, with source-level and measurement limitations.
claims.excerpt: Space: category, app/tool-owner, project, folder and large-file views ... Native sampling groups helpers through parent/app relationships ... Path-derived ownership and sampled writes are not proof of the writer of a specific file
claims.conditions: Read capabilities.md cited implementation paths. Partial/permission-limited inventory, sampled accounting, no guaranteed savings or fault diagnosis. Not proof of hardware testing or volume repair.

claims.wording: Hosted AI needs internet and authentication; AI Care is advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year, renewing with applicable tax. Free local tools are distinct from hosted AI.
claims.excerpt: Hosted AI assistance requires internet access and authentication ... $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year ... Plans renew until cancelled; applicable tax shown at checkout.
claims.conditions: Relevant paths/process/storage data can reach service and Cloudflare Workers AI. Exact AI quotas/payment enforcement unverified; no entirely-offline AI claim. Website free-account download gate differs from public GitHub downloads.

claims.wording: Breathing Room daily care reuses exact saved approvals while the app runs; the optional interactive Ruff automatic mode must be distinguished from ordinary approval.
claims.excerpt: Saved approvals bind account, API origin, action method/path and native rule; new actions wait for review ... Automatically move verified Ruff lint caches to Trash ... App must remain running
claims.conditions: Not blanket future authority or safety guarantee. Trash moves do not equal immediate available-space recovery.

article.proposedTitle: Low Mac storage or a damaged volume? Choose the right investigation
article.primaryIntent: Help a Mac owner separate capacity/growth investigation from hardware/volume-integrity diagnosis before choosing a maintenance tool.
article.leadDirection: Storage size and volume integrity answer different questions. Use storage attribution for capacity questions; choose a documented diagnostic workflow for suspected volume/hardware problems. Neither cleanup nor a normal test result guarantees healthy hardware or recoverable data.
outline: Top visual: licensed/approved Techtool test view, not box art
Distinguish capacity, recurring writes and volume integrity; do not diagnose from low space alone
Map each question to documented tests versus storage views; separate testing from repair/erase
Read APFS support qualifications before assuming full rebuild or optimization
Use the labeled Breathing Room Space preview to explain inventory, rebuild/download costs and exact approval scope
One disclosed recommendation: Breathing Room, which we build, may fit attribution/cleanup; Techtool Pro fits documented diagnostics; neither is a proven full substitute
Installation, hosted-data and update/licensing caveats; link the concise comparison
article.interactionHandoff: Non-executing three-choice decision aid: capacity question -> inventory/review; repeated growth -> activity with attribution caveat; integrity/hardware concern -> backup-aware diagnostics/support. Do not infer failing hardware or trigger scanning, repair, deletion, sign-in or email.
article.notATutorial: No commands, demo repository, measurements or hands-on claims. Actual repair procedure would require version-specific manual and separate evidence.
article.links: Proposed /comparisons/techtool/ and /comparisons/; draft job must verify routes exist. No invented tool link.
